I found a plan that misses no episodes and costs 4 periods (1099 + 1199 + 899 + 1799 = 4996 cents, $49.96).

**Viewing windows** (release date through release + 14 days)

| Title | Service | Window | Paid period | Access |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| The Amber Harbor (all 8 episodes) | Orbit | Dec 17 – Dec 31 | starts 2026-12-17 | Dec 17 – Jan 17 |
| The Salt Archive (all 10 episodes) | Northline | Dec 27 – Jan 10 | starts 2026-12-27 | Dec 27 – Jan 27 |
| The Velvet Kingdom (weekly, 7 episodes) | Tidewell | Ep 1: Jan 7 – Jan 21; Ep 7: Feb 18 – Mar 4 | starts 2027-01-21 | Jan 21 – Feb 21 |
| The Distant Atlas (all 7 episodes) | Kestrel+ | Feb 22 – Mar 8 | starts 2027-02-22 | Feb 22 – Mar 22 |

**Why one Tidewell period is enough:** starting on Jan 21 catches the last day of episode 1's window. It also reaches Feb 18–20, which falls inside episode 7's window. Episodes 2–6 have windows in between, so they are covered as well.

**Already-paid access:** Northline (to Nov 19), Tidewell (to Nov 24) and Lumen (to Nov 13) are not needed for any title, so they lapse at no cost. Lumen and Marquee are never used.

**Rule checks:**
- **Overlap:** the new Northline and Tidewell periods start well after their paid-through dates, so nothing is paid twice.
- **Concurrent limit:** at most 3 services are active on any day. In November the three already-paid services coexist, but they don't exceed 3 and no new period starts then. From December on, at most 2 overlap (for example Orbit and Northline from Dec 27 to Jan 17).
- **Cost:** there are four separate titles on four services, and each needs one period, so 4 periods is the lowest possible cost.
